seat.BEST_WHY: The floor masonry is the strongest thing in the deck and 4 carries it without the placement fault that 3 has. Under and right of the figure (x≈430–700, y≈480–640) the blocks run in courses of unequal length — a long block at (600–700, 590–630) sits over two short ones — and the joints are drawn as dark 2px stubs that stop and restart rather than a continuous grid, so the floor reads as laid, not stamped. The pillar at (265–300, 540–640) has a pale top face, a darker front face, and a rope band at its foot that sits on the front face, not floating over it. The A-frame brace at (580–680, 400–455) has its feet on the wall base line and both pairs of flanking pins sit on the rail at the same height. The corridor-corner wedge at (505–540, 390–440) is a lit timber board with a bright top edge that continues the rail, so it reads as a leaning plank instead of a blank diagonal.
seat.WORST_WHY: Nothing in it is lit. The figure at (205–245, 0–30) carries no light; the dirt at the top-left and the dirt at the bottom-right are the same value. The grey wall-top tiles (e.g. the column at x 0–70, y 0–150 and the run along y 190–240) are identical 24px stamps with a 1px seam grid and no bevel, shadow or edge against the water or dirt beside them, so they read as floor, not as the top of something with height. The water at (250–380, 0–190) is a flat teal fill with a hexagon-lattice pattern repeated edge to edge at constant value — a screen-fill, not a surface. The moss at (25–60, 65–100) and (200–235, 75–105) is flat teal blobs with a 1px outline. The dirt tile repeats visibly at 48px (the dark blotch cluster at (100–140, 30–60) recurs at (100–140, 80–110)). The orc's sword blade is clipped by the top edge of the frame.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08
panel.seat_plant_stop: 3 seats missed a live plant in one round (seats 1, 2, 3). That is not one seat having a bad day.

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.

item_exit.measured: MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING (tools/cast_shadows/evidence/jamb/, m_flat + jamb_m_shadow). (b) The cap's upper half was re-laid over the prop (cap_bands_over_props=2) — the law says never. (c) Flat-lit wood albedo: Λ (84,62,42) vs X (91,66,44), same hue ratios (r/g 1.36/1.38, g/b 1.45/1.49) — one wood. At the regime Λ reads L 73 r/g 1.74 against X's 47/1.63 because Λ is 1.4 tiles from the fire (reach 4.0) and X 6.3 — not the same fire. FIX: shift = cell − margin − PropBaseRun (one constant, shared with the occluder), so the base's far edge meets the foot and its near edge sits 11 px onto the floor; the cap-band re-lay removed.
